channel.title: Local News Wire Broadcast Feed
channel.description: Approved local stories in broadcast order

item.description: Vermont business leaders say rising costs are squeezing tourism and hospitality. Killington Resort saw ski visits rise six percent but food and drink sales fall over ten percent per visitor. The resort built nearly four hundred subsidized housing units for workers and remains profitable.

Elizabethtown in Essex County secured twenty-four million dollars in state funds for a new public sewer system. The project addresses wastewater contamination, including E. coli found in local waters. Construction is planned to start in late twenty-twenty-eight or early twenty-twenty-nine.

The Charles R. Wood Foundation gave ten thousand dollars to Silver Bay YMCA's early learning center in Ticonderoga. The center serves children from six weeks to five years and supports mostly low-income working families. Enrollment is open now to help sustain this important childcare resource.

Rutland Housing Authority addressed safety concerns at Sheldon Towers after a recent fire and drug bust. The building houses seniors and disabled residents, with many previously homeless. Security cameras and police patrols are in place, but evicting problem tenants takes time due to legal protections.
